messages.subject: Dealing with NA observations and binned analyses
parts:
Hi all,

 I’m performing distance analysis to obtain density estimates for a species in R using the ds() function. I have raw data of the following form:


Region.Label / Sample.Label / Effort / FieldLabel / Habitat / distbegin / distend / Count

BR22 1 80 A Arable 0 25      1
BR22 1 80 A Arable 25 100      5
BR22 1 80 A Arable 100 200      NA
BR22 1 80 B Grass 0 25      1
BR22 1 80 B Grass 25 100      NA
BR22 1 80 B Grass 100 200      2
BR22 2 120 C Arable 0 25      NA
BR22 2 120 C Arable 25 100      NA
BR22 2 120 C Arable 100 200      NA


I first make each count into a single row (e.g. there will be five identical rows for location BR22, transect 1, field A, distbegin 25, distend 100), but then I am not exactly sure how to deal with the NA rows. I have put two possibilities below.

Data for ds() model in R (version 1): in this version I ignore the NA rows for transect 1, fields A and B as we have counts from other distance bins, and I include one NA row for transect 2, field C:

BR22 1 80 A Arable 0 25         1
BR22 1 80 A Arable 25 100         1
BR22 1 80 A Arable 25 100    1
BR22 1 80 A Arable 25 100  1
BR22 1 80 A Arable 25 100         1
BR22 1 80 A Arable 25 100  1
BR22 1 80 B Grass 0 25     1
BR22 1 80 B Grass 100 200  1
BR22 1 80 B Grass 100 200  1
BR22 2 120 C Arable NA NA         NA


Data for ds() model in R (version 2): in this version I include NA rows for transect 1, fields A and B to account for the NAs from certain distance bands, and I include one NA row for transect 2, field C:

BR22 1 80 A Arable 0 25    1
BR22 1 80 A Arable 25 100  1
BR22 1 80 A Arable 25 100  1
BR22 1 80 A Arable 25 100  1
BR22 1 80 A Arable 25 100  1
BR22 1 80 A Arable 25 100  1
BR22 1 80 A Arable NA NA    NA
BR22 1 80 B Grass 0 25    1
BR22 1 80 B Grass NA NA   NA
BR22 1 80 B Grass 100 200   1
BR22 1 80 B Grass 100 200  1
BR22 2 120 C Arable NA NA          NA


My feeling is that version 1 would be the correct way to deal with the NA observations, but I’m second guessing myself now! Any help and advice will be greatly appreciated.

 

Thank you,

Charlotte.

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Dealing with NA observations and binned analyses
parts:
Charlotte

Thanks for your question. Your instinct (believing version 1 to be correct) is accurate.

The "ds" function is deriving two distinct pieces of information from the data frame provided to it: a) information about distances (in your case bins) to detected objects and b) (equally important) information about survey design. It is through the use of NAs that complete information about the survey design is passed to "ds".  

By referring to "survey design" what I mean is information about numbers of strata, transects within strata and effort associated with those transects. Note, that I do not include "distance bins" as relating to "survey design". Those bins only serve a purpose in the detection function model fitting. Hence, there is no need to have an entry in the data frame for each bin of each transect (as you show in your original table).  Therefore, your "verison 1" data frame contains necessary information about the survey design; with the row for transect 2 in field C. That row must exist for complete survey design information to be available to "ds". However, without detections on that transect, the fields distbegin, distend and count need to be populated with NA.

As an aside, I see in your "version 0", you have count values >= 1, whereas for your "version 1" data frame, you have changed transect 1 of stratum A to be five detections of single birds within the 25-100 bin. These are two ways of dealing with animals that occur in groups; the two approaches should produce equivalent estimates, see
  • Buckland, S.T., Plumptre, A.J., Thomas, L. et al. Design and Analysis of Line Transect Surveys for Primates. Int J Primatol 31, 833–847 (2010). https://doi.org/10.1007/s10764-010-9431-5
